avertissement: The definitions in this glossary are written by DossierBC — they are not the City of Vancouver’s texts nor legal definitions. What comes from the official record is the count of occurrences and the example under each term.

entrees.definition: The Mayor and ten Councillors, all elected city-wide for four years. Council decides by motion: the question is put, each member votes, and the motion is carried or lost.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: The meeting type on most cards. Vancouver has no wards: every member represents the whole city.

entrees.definition: A Council meeting held on the regular schedule, where reports, by-laws and motions are decided.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: A meeting type in the City’s record.

entrees.definition: A Council meeting called outside the regular schedule, usually for one matter.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: A meeting type in the City’s record.

exemple.objet: Continuing the Success of the Granville Street Pedestrian Zone Pilot and Temporary Patios throughout the City - final motion as amended

entrees.definition: Council sitting to hear speakers before deciding on rezoning, heritage and certain other by-laws. The vote at the end of a hearing is a Council vote.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Most rezoning decisions are made at a public hearing, often late in the evening.

entrees.aussi: Policy & Strategic Priorities; City Finance & Services
entrees.definition: A committee made up of all Council members that hears staff reports and speakers first. Its decisions are referred to the next Council meeting to be made final.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Two of Vancouver’s meeting types. The same item can therefore be voted twice: once in committee, once in Council.

exemple.objet: Motion 14. Policy Framework for Overdose Prevention and Harm Reduction Facilities

entrees.definition: Council sitting as a court to hear appeals about local improvement charges and parcel taxes.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: A rare meeting type in the City’s record.

entrees.definition: The Council committee that oversees the City’s independent Auditor General.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: A rare meeting type in the City’s record.

entrees.definition: Elected city-wide. Chairs Council meetings and votes like every other member.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: One line per vote in the City’s record, like the ten Councillors.

entrees.definition: One of ten members elected city-wide. No Councillor represents a neighbourhood: each one represents all of Vancouver.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: The City writes the title, an initial and the family name: “Councillor P Fry”.

entrees.definition: A vote in which each member’s choice is written down. Since 2016 Vancouver records every Council vote electronically, member by member — in many councils a recorded vote has to be requested.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Every card on this site. The City notes that the official record remains the meeting minutes.

entrees.definition: The member voted for the motion.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: The “for” count on each card.

entrees.definition: The member voted against the motion.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: The “against” count, and the names under “Against”.

entrees.definition: The member was present and did not vote for or against. The record gives the status, not the reason.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Listed under “Abstained” when a card is opened.

entrees.definition: The member was not in the room when this vote was taken.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Listed under “Absent” when a card is opened. Absence from one vote is not absence from the meeting.

entrees.definition: The member declared a conflict of interest on this item, left the room and did not vote.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: The gold tag on a card and on a member’s profile. The rarest status in the record.

exemple.objet: Decision Re: Integrity Commissioner Investigation Report

entrees.definition: The member was not eligible to vote on this item. The record gives the status, not the reason.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Rare. Shown when a card is opened.

entrees.definition: No vote was registered for the member. The City changed the definition of this status on September 21, 2021; see its change log.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Rare in recent years.

entrees.definition: More members voted for the motion than against it: it passed.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: The result tag on a card.

entrees.definition: Every member who voted was in favour.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: The most common result. Unanimous does not mean everyone was present.

entrees.definition: The motion did not get a majority: it failed.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: The red result tag. Often an amendment or a member’s motion.

exemple.objet: CD-1 Rezoning: 2345-2349 Main Street - Withdrawal Motion on the Main Motion

entrees.definition: The question Council votes on. A staff report’s recommendations, a by-law, or a member’s own proposal become a motion once moved and seconded.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Every card is one motion put to a vote.

entrees.definition: A motion to change the wording of the motion on the floor. It is voted first; if it carries, the main motion is then voted as amended.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: A card whose subject ends with “– Amendment”. The same item then appears again as the main motion.

entrees.definition: A motion to send the matter to staff, to a committee or to a later meeting instead of deciding now.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: A card whose subject ends with “– Referral”.

exemple.objet: Motion 6 - Protecting and Planning Vancouver's Waterfront Precinct - Referred

entrees.definition: A City law. Council votes to enact it after a report and, for zoning and heritage, after a public hearing.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Enactment votes, often several at once near the end of a Council meeting.

exemple.objet: Item 2. Modification to Conditions of Approval and By-law Enactment for 450-496 Prior Street, 550 Malkin Avenue, 1002 Station Street and 1050 Gore Ave

entrees.definition: Items brought by a Councillor or the Mayor rather than by staff, raised at the end of a meeting.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: A card whose subject starts with “NEW BUSINESS”.

entrees.definition: Changing which uses and buildings are allowed on a site, by amending the Zoning and Development By-law. Decided after a public hearing.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: The most frequent subject at public hearings, usually with the street address.

entrees.definition: A zoning district written for one site, with its own rules, instead of a standard zone that applies across the city.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: “CD-1 Rezoning: 5229-5249 Ash Street”.

entrees.definition: A change to the wording of a zoning district’s rules, rather than to the zoning map.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Public hearing items without a single address.

exemple.objet: Item 5. CD-1 (708) Text Amendment: 2538-2550 Birch Street and 1290-1298 West Broadway

entrees.definition: Legal protection of a building or site by by-law. Changes to it then need a heritage alteration permit.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Public hearing items that pair a heritage by-law with a rezoning.

entrees.definition: The City’s approval of a specific building project under the zoning that already applies. Most are decided by staff; Council sees policy and appeals.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Occasionally in Council items about process and timelines.

entrees.definition: Money the City gives to an organization for a stated purpose. Council approves grants, often by the dozen in one report.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Items from Arts, Culture and Community Services.

exemple.objet: Arts, Culture and Community Services Sublease, Lease and Licence Agreements and Grant Approvals

entrees.definition: The City renting out, or renting, a property. A licence agreement gives a right to use a space without a lease.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Real estate items, often bundled with grants to community groups.

exemple.objet: Arts, Culture and Community Services Sublease, Lease and Licence Agreements and Grant Approvals

entrees.definition: The yearly auction of properties whose property taxes have been unpaid for years. Council can cancel a sale.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: A short Council item each fall.

entrees.definition: The multi-year plan of what the City will build, buy and repair, and the yearly budget that funds it.
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Finance committee and Council items, mostly in the fall and winter.

entrees.aussi: Development Cost Levies; Community Amenity Contributions
entrees.definition: What developers pay the City when they build: a levy set by by-law (DCL), and a contribution negotiated with a rezoning (CAC).
entrees.ouVousLeVoyez: Rezoning reports and by-law updates.
